outcome: prevalence of sickle cell disease in pregnancy
risk factors for morbidity and mortality in women with SCD
cohort: Pregnant women with and without sickle cell disease who gave birth between 1999 and 2008, identified from the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project Nationwide Inpatient Sample (HCUP-NIS)
finding: Pregnant women with sickle cell disease have a high risk of morbidity and mortality, which is further increased by the development of acute sickle cell crisis.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates were higher in women with SCD.
